claim_1.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy YFV-seronegative volunteers after a single YF-17D vaccination (day 0) showed rapid and broad transcriptional changes, with 1001 differentially expressed genes overall, 146 genes altered at 4 h after vaccination (day 0), peaks in DEG numbers at days 2 and 5, and return toward baseline by day 28 compared to prevaccination baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: YF-17D vaccination induced broad transcriptional changes, as evidenced by the finding that 1001 significantly differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were modulated at least one time-point postvaccination as compared to their prevaccination levels (Supplemental Table 1).
At the earliest time-point postvaccination (4 h), 146 genes were identified as significantly up (36 genes) or down (110 genes) regulated.

Thus, the PBMC transcriptome responded to vaccination very rapidly (within hours after vaccination), and some in a transient manner. The number of DEGs changes peaked at Days 2 and 5, and then returned to baseline levels at Day 28 (Figure 1A).

comparison.finding: Compared to prevaccination baseline at day 0, the number of differentially expressed genes peaked at day 2 as part of rapid and broad transcriptional changes after YF-17D vaccination.
Compared to prevaccination baseline at day 0, the number of differentially expressed genes peaked at day 5 as part of rapid and broad transcriptional changes after YF-17D vaccination.
By day 28, transcriptional changes returned toward baseline compared to prevaccination baseline at day 0.

claim_2.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy YFV-seronegative volunteers after a single YF-17D vaccination (day 0) showed that inhibited pathways were already detectable at 4 h after vaccination (day 0), including PRR, TNF receptor-mediated, TREM-1, and IL-6/IL-1 pathways, while PPAR-mediated and LXR/RXR activation pathways were maximally activated at 4 h after vaccination (day 0) compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: The top inhibited pathways, defined by drastic gene downregulation sustained over two weeks postvaccination, included the pattern recognition receptor (PRR), TNF receptor-mediated, TREM-1, and IL-6/IL-1 pathways.

Meanwhile, the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR)-mediated pathway, which plays essential roles in the regulation of cellular differentiation, development, and metabolism (carbohydrate, lipid, protein) (37, 38), and the LXR/RXR activation pathway were activated to their maximum extent at 4 h; this activation persisted over the entire time course.

comparison.finding: At 4 h after vaccination versus baseline on day 0, PRR, TNF receptor-mediated, TREM-1, and IL-6/IL-1 pathways were inhibited, while PPAR-mediated and LXR/RXR activation pathways were maximally activated.

claim_3.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy YFV-seronegative volunteers after a single YF-17D vaccination (day 0) showed interferon signaling was the most highly activated pathway, with strongest activation on days 2, 5, and 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: As expected by its critical antiviral role, the most highly activated pathway after YF-17D vaccination was the interferon signaling pathway (Figure 2).
Consistent with the expression of individual genes involved in interferon signaling (Figure 1), this pathway was highly activated on Days 2, 5, and 7.

comparison.finding: interferon signaling was highly activated on day 2 compared to baseline day 0
interferon signaling was highly activated on day 5 compared to baseline day 0
interferon signaling was highly activated on day 7 compared to baseline day 0

claim_4.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from 21 healthy YFV-seronegative volunteers after a single YF-17D vaccination (day 0) showed blood transcription module responses peaked at day 5 and day 7, with innate immune modules enriched on days 2, 5, and 7 and B-cell-related modules enriched at day 14 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: For example, the module responses peaked at Day 5 (15 upregulated modules), waned by Day 7 (6 upregulated modules), and returned to the baseline level by Day 28 (Figure 3).

Modules induced by YF-17D vaccination were associated with the innate immune response (e.g. antiviral type I interferon signature, activated dendritic cells, RIG-1 like receptor signaling, chemokines, complement activation, IRF2-targeting network, and FOSL) at Days 2, 5 and 7.

Concomitantly, the cell division/cycle progression relative critical regulator PLK1 signaling and B cell related modules (e.g. memory B cell surface signature, plasma cell and immunoglobulin) were enriched at Day 14, indicating enhanced humoral immunological responses.

comparison.finding: innate immune modules, including antiviral type I interferon signature, activated dendritic cells, RIG-1 like receptor signaling, chemokines, complement activation, IRF2-targeting network, and FOSL, were enriched at day 2 versus baseline

blood transcription module responses peaked at day 5, with innate immune modules including antiviral type I interferon signature, activated dendritic cells, RIG-1 like receptor signaling, chemokines, complement activation, IRF2-targeting network, and FOSL enriched versus baseline

blood transcription module responses remained elevated at day 7, with innate immune modules including antiviral type I interferon signature, activated dendritic cells, RIG-1 like receptor signaling, chemokines, complement activation, IRF2-targeting network, and FOSL enriched versus baseline
B-cell-related modules, including memory B cell surface signature, plasma cell and immunoglobulin modules, as well as PLK1 signaling, were enriched at day 14 versus baseline

claim_5.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from vaccinated participants showed innate-cell frequencies changed after YF-17D vaccination (day 0): monocytes decreased at day 14 and increased by day 86, CD11c+ and CD123+ dendritic cells increased at day 86, and plasmacytoid dendritic cells increased at days 7 and 28 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Regarding innate immune cells, compared to baseline levels at 0 h, the percentage of monocytes in PBMCs decreased significantly at Day 14 (p = 0.01) after a negligible change at Day 7, and later increased at Day 86 (p = 0.095) (Figure 4A).

The percentage of DCs fluctuated postvaccination, with the percentages of CD11c+ (Figure 4B) and CD123+ (Figure 4C) cells significantly increased at Day 86 vs. 0 h, and the percentage of plasmacytoid DCs (CD123+) also significantly increased at Days 7 and 28 vs. 0 h.

comparison.finding: monocytes decreased significantly at day 14 vs day 0
monocytes increased by day 86 vs day 0; CD11c+ dendritic cells and CD123+ dendritic cells significantly increased at day 86 vs day 0
plasmacytoid dendritic cells (CD123+) significantly increased at day 7 vs day 0
plasmacytoid dendritic cells (CD123+) significantly increased at day 28 vs day 0

claim_6.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from vaccinated participants showed overall NK-cell percentages decreased after YF-17D vaccination, including activated NKp46 and inhibitory NKG2A marker-defined NK cells, compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Generally, the percentage of NK cells decreased after vaccination, with the same trend for both activated (NKp46) (Figure 4F) and inhibitory (NKG2A) (Figure 4E) markers.

comparison.finding: overall NK-cell percentages decreased after YF-17D vaccination compared to baseline, including activated NKp46 and inhibitory NKG2A marker-defined NK cells

claim_7.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from vaccinated participants in an NK-mediated ADCC functional assay showed NK-mediated cytotoxicity, measured by ADCC activity and TNF-α, IFN-γ, and CD107a secretion, increased significantly at day 7 after YF-17D vaccination (day 0) and returned to baseline at and after day 14 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: NK-mediated cytotoxicity, as assessed by ADCC activity or secretion of the cytokines TNF-α, IFN-γ, and CD107a, increased significantly at Day 7 and dropped to baseline levels at and after Day 14 (Figure 4 G-I).

comparison.finding: NK-mediated cytotoxicity, measured by ADCC activity and TNF-α, IFN-γ, and CD107a secretion, increased significantly at day 7 compared to baseline
NK-mediated cytotoxicity, measured by ADCC activity and TNF-α, IFN-γ, and CD107a secretion, returned to baseline at day 14 compared to baseline

claim_8.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from vaccinated participants showed B-cell populations increased after YF-17D vaccination (day 0), with total B cells elevated at day 14 and remaining high through days 28 and 86, mature B cells increased after day 7 through day 86, IgM-only memory B cells increased from day 28 to day 86, and class-switched memory B cells decreased at day 7 then recovered by day 86 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Flow cytometry staining of PBMCs revealed that B cell populations increased at Day 14 vs. Day 0 (p = 0.021) and persisted at high levels for 3 months (p = 0.029 and 0.02 at Day 28 and Day 86, respectively), as shown in Figure 5.
Similar to the overall B cell populations, the mature B cell population (IgD+ IgM+) increased after Day 7 (p < 0.001) and remained at a high level until Day 86 (p < 0.001) (Figure 5 B).
The IgM-only memory B cells (IgD- IgM + CD27+) showed a significant boost from Day 28 to Day 86 (Figure 5 C).
The percentage of class-switched memory B cells (IgD- IgG- CD27+) (shown in Figure 5 D) slightly decreased at Day 7 but recovered by Day 86.

comparison.finding: total B cells increased at day 14 compared to day 0
total B cells remained elevated at day 28 compared to day 0
total B cells remained elevated at day 86 compared to day 0
class-switched memory B cells slightly decreased at day 7 compared to baseline day 0
class-switched memory B cells recovered by day 86 compared to baseline day 0
mature B cells increased after day 7 compared to day 0
mature B cells remained increased through day 86 compared to day 0
IgM-only memory B cells increased from day 28 to day 86

claim_9.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from vaccinated participants showed CD4+ and CD8+ T cells expressing CD28 and Ki67 decreased at day 7 after YF-17D vaccination (day 0) compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: The percentages of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells expressing CD28 and Ki67 decreased (p < 0.001, p = 0.03, p < 0.001, p = 0.001, respectively) at Day 7 vs. Day 0 (shown in Figure 5 E-H), implying that T cell proliferation was unexpectedly suppressed by vaccination.

comparison.finding: percentages of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells expressing CD28 and Ki67 decreased at day 7 versus day 0

claim_10.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from vaccinated participants after stimulation with YFV NS1 or Env peptide pools showed YFV-specific IL-2 secretion by CD4+ cells increased at day 28 and day 86 after YF-17D vaccination (day 0) compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: This analysis revealed that secretion of YFV-specific IL-2 by CD4+ cells (as shown in Figure 5 I, J) increased at Day 28 and Day 86 post vaccination after stimulation with NS1 and Env antigens, respectively (p = 0.07 and p = 0.038).

comparison.finding: YFV-specific IL-2 secretion by CD4+ cells increased at day 28 compared to baseline after stimulation with YFV NS1 peptide pools
YFV-specific IL-2 secretion by CD4+ cells increased at day 86 compared to baseline after stimulation with YFV Env peptide pools

claim_11.claim: immunofluorescence assay analysis of baseline serum from 21 subjects showed 6 of 21 were seropositive to at least one of the tested flaviviruses, WNV or JEV.

sources.quote: We therefore performed immunofluorescence assays to investigate baseline serum reactivity to West Nile Virus (WNV) and Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV). We found that six out of the 21 subjects were seropositive to at least one of the flaviviruses tested (Supplemental Figure 3).

claim_12.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs showed that after YF-17D vaccination (day 0), WNV/JEV-seronegative participants had higher percentages of myeloid dendritic cells from day 14 through day 86 than WNV/JEV-seropositive participants, whereas WNV/JEV-seropositive participants had higher NK activity at days 7, 28, and 86.

sources.quote: The percentage of myeloid dendritic cells was higher in WNV/JEV-seronegative participants from Day 14 through Day 86 post vaccination compared to WNV/JEV-seropositive participants (Figure 6A).
Interestingly, WNV/JEV-seropositive volunteers showed higher levels of NK activity than WNV/JEV-seronegative participants at Days 7, 28, and 86 postvaccination (Figure 6B).

comparison.finding: WNV/JEV-seropositive participants had higher NK activity at day 7 than WNV/JEV-seronegative participants
WNV/JEV-seronegative participants had higher percentages of myeloid dendritic cells at day 14 than WNV/JEV-seropositive participants

WNV/JEV-seronegative participants had higher percentages of myeloid dendritic cells at day 28 than WNV/JEV-seropositive participants; WNV/JEV-seropositive participants had higher NK activity at day 28 than WNV/JEV-seronegative participants

WNV/JEV-seronegative participants had higher percentages of myeloid dendritic cells at day 86 than WNV/JEV-seropositive participants; WNV/JEV-seropositive participants had higher NK activity at day 86 than WNV/JEV-seronegative participants

claim_13.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs showed that after YF-17D vaccination (day 0), IFN-γ secretion was significantly enhanced in WNV/JEV-seropositive individuals, whereas TNF-α secretion was enhanced in WNV/JEV-seronegative participants.

sources.quote: Figure 6D shows CD4+ and CD8+ cytokine secretion by baseline flavivirus serostatus. Interestingly, IFN-γ secretion was significantly enhanced in WNV/JEV-seropositive individuals, whereas TNF-α secretion was enhanced in WNV/JEV-seronegative participants (Figure 6D).

comparison.finding: IFN-γ secretion was significantly enhanced in WNV/JEV-seropositive individuals, whereas TNF-α secretion was enhanced in WNV/JEV-seronegative participants at day 0 after YF-17D vaccination

claim_14.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis integrating day-7 gene expression with immunological traits showed the Turquoise module was most strongly associated with CD14+ macrophage cells and myeloid DC cells, the Green module with B cells and CD28++ CD8+ T cells, the Brown module with memory B cells, the Blue module with CD8+ T-cell CD28, and the Yellow module with myeloid DCs.

sources.quote: The highest MS scores observed were for the Turquoise module with CD14+ macrophage cells (MS = 0.87, p = 2e-7) and myeloid DC cells (MS = 0.69, p = 6e-4), in addition to the Green module with B cells (MS = 0.65, p = 0.001) and CD28++ CD8+ T cells (MS = 0.5, p = 0.02).

In addition, the Brown module had a high score for memory B cells (IgD- IgM+ CD27+) (MS = 0.47, p = 0.03). The Blue module was significantly related to the CD8+ T subset proliferation marker CD28 (MS = 0.52, p = 0.01), whereas the Yellow module was associated with myeloid DCs (MS = 0.51, p = 0.02).

claim_15.claim: Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay analysis of plasma/sera measured anti-YFV neutralizing antibodies by PRNT after vaccination, but no explicit Results-section quantitative finding from the main text pages was provided.

sources.quote: Anti-YFV neutralizing antibodies were measured by the plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT).
